Let one but read that blessed list, realizing that it shows not only the largeness and heartiness of Paul’s sympathy, but also the special care which the Holy Spirit has for each individual member of the household of faith, singling them out by name, and there will be no questioning as to why such things were written.

But one thing is very significant, and that is the fact that there is no mention of Peter, who is claimed to have been “the first Bishop of Rome.” We may sometimes learn as much by what the Bible does not say as by what it does say. From what is not said in this place we may learn that so far from being Bishop of Rome, Peter was not in Rome at all when Paul wrote, and that if he was ever in Rome it was after the Epistle to the Romans was written, and long after the church was established and flourishing there. For it is most certain that in saluting the members of the church by name Paul would not have omitted the name of the chief person in it, whose hospitality he had once shared in Jerusalem for fifteen days. Of course there is abundance of the most positive evidence that neither the church of Christ nor the church of Rome was founded upon Peter; but if there were no other, this testimony of the sixteenth chapter of Romans would be sufficient to settle the matter.

entries.author: E.J. Waggoner
entries.text: In Conclusion.-“Now to him that is of power to stablish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began, but now is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith; to God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.” R.V.

entries.author: E.J. Waggoner
entries.text: What a magnificent conclusion! It reaches from eternity to eternity. The Gospel of God is the thing of the ages. It was kept secret in the mind of God from times eternal. Christ “was foreordained before the foundation of the world.” 1 Peter 1:19, 20. But now the mystery is “made manifest.” Not simply is it made manifest by the preaching of the apostles, but “according to the commandment of the everlasting God,” “by the scriptures of the prophets” it is “made known to all nations, for the obedience of faith.” The Gospel plan originated in the mind of God in the eternity of the past. Patriarchs, prophets and apostles have worked in unison in making it manifest; and “in the ages to come” it will be both the science and the song of the redeemed “of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues,” who shall gather with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of God, and will say, “Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, and hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father, to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.”

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Spiritual Blessings in Christ**

**Themes:** Election, Redemption, Sealed with the Holy Spirit, Paul's Prayer for Spiritual Wisdom

**Outline:**
1. Greetings (1:1-2)
2. Spiritual Blessings (1:3-14)
3. Prayer for Revelation (1:15-23)

**Summary:**
Paul begins by praising God for the spiritual blessings given to believers in Christ, emphasizing predestination, redemption, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit. He concludes with a prayer for the Ephesians to have spiritual wisdom and to understand the great power of God demonstrated in Christ's resurrection.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Saved by Grace Through Faith**

**Themes:** Grace, Salvation, Unity of Jews and Gentiles in Christ

**Outline:**
1. From Death to Life (2:1-10)
2. One in Christ (2:11-22)

**Summary:**
Paul explains that believers are saved by grace through faith, not by their own works, having been brought from spiritual death to life. He then illustrates how Christ has broken down the dividing wall of hostility between Jews and Gentiles, uniting them into one new humanity and a dwelling place for God.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Mystery of the Gospel Revealed**

**Themes:** The Mystery of Christ, Paul's Ministry to the Gentiles, Prayer for Spiritual Strength

**Outline:**
1. Paul's Ministry of the Mystery (3:1-13)
2. Prayer for Spiritual Empowerment (3:14-21)

**Summary:**
Paul describes his calling to preach the 'mystery' of Christ—that Gentiles are fellow heirs and members of the same body. He prays that the Ephesians may be strengthened by the Spirit and rooted in the immeasurable love of Christ, ending with a doxology praising God's power.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Unity and the New Life**

**Themes:** Unity in the Body of Christ, Spiritual Gifts, The Old vs. New Self

**Outline:**
1. Unity in the Body (4:1-16)
2. Living as Children of Light (4:17-32)

**Summary:**
Paul urges believers to live worthy of their calling, maintaining the unity of the Spirit. He lists the spiritual gifts given to build up the church. He then contrasts their former way of life with the new life in Christ, instructing them to put away falsehood, anger, and bitterness, and instead be kind and forgiving.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Walking in Love and Light**

**Themes:** Imitating God, Light vs. Darkness, Spirit-Filled Living, Christian Marriage

**Outline:**
1. Walk in Love (5:1-7)
2. Walk in Light (5:8-14)
3. Walk in Wisdom (5:15-21)
4. Instructions for Wives and Husbands (5:22-33)

**Summary:**
Believers are called to imitate God and walk in love, avoiding sexual immorality and impurity. They are to live as children of light, exposing darkness, and being filled with the Spirit. Paul then provides instructions on mutual submission, specifically detailing the roles of husbands and wives as a reflection of Christ and the church.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Armor of God**

**Themes:** Children and Parents, Slaves and Masters, Spiritual Warfare, The Armor of God

**Outline:**
1. Instructions for Children and Parents (6:1-4)
2. Instructions for Slaves and Masters (6:5-9)
3. The Armor of God (6:10-20)
4. Final Greetings (6:21-24)

**Summary:**
After addressing relationships between children and parents, and slaves and masters, Paul transitions to spiritual warfare. He commands believers to put on the full armor of God to stand firm against the devil's schemes. He concludes the letter with final greetings and a blessing of peace and grace.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**To Live is Christ**

**Themes:** Thanksgiving, Joy in Suffering, Advancing the Gospel, To Live is Christ

**Outline:**
1. Greetings and Prayer (1:1-11)
2. Paul's Imprisonment Advances the Gospel (1:12-18)
3. To Live is Christ, to Die is Gain (1:19-30)

**Summary:**
Paul expresses profound gratitude and joy for the Philippians' partnership in the gospel. He explains that his imprisonment has actually served to advance the gospel message. Torn between a desire to depart and be with Christ or remain in the flesh for their progress, he encourages them to live in a manner worthy of the gospel.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Humility and Exaltation of Christ**

**Themes:** Humility, Christ's Example, Shining as Lights, Timothy and Epaphroditus

**Outline:**
1. Imitating Christ's Humility (2:1-11)
2. Lights in the World (2:12-18)
3. Commendation of Timothy and Epaphroditus (2:19-30)

**Summary:**
Paul urges unity through humility, presenting the ultimate example: Jesus Christ, who emptied himself to become a servant and died on a cross, leading to His exaltation. Paul exhorts believers to work out their salvation and shine as lights. He also commends his co-workers, Timothy and Epaphroditus, for their faithful service.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Pressing Toward the Mark**

**Themes:** Righteousness Through Faith, Knowing Christ, Straining Toward the Goal, Heavenly Citizenship

**Outline:**
1. Righteousness Through Faith (3:1-11)
2. Pressing on Toward the Goal (3:12-16)
3. Citizenship in Heaven (3:17-21)

**Summary:**
Warning against false teachers who rely on the flesh and the law, Paul counts all his previous accomplishments as loss compared to knowing Christ. He describes his pursuit of knowing Christ and the power of His resurrection, pressing on toward the heavenly prize. He reminds believers that their true citizenship is in heaven.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Rejoice in the Lord Always**

**Themes:** Joy, Peace, Right Thinking, Contentment, God's Provision

**Outline:**
1. Exhortations to Unity and Joy (4:1-9)
2. Paul's Thanks for Their Gifts (4:10-20)
3. Final Greetings (4:21-23)

**Summary:**
Paul exhorts the Philippians to stand firm, resolve conflicts, and rejoice in the Lord always. He encourages them to bring their anxieties to God in prayer to experience His peace, and to focus their minds on whatever is true and good. He thanks them for their financial support, expressing his contentment in all circumstances through Christ's strength.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Supremacy of Christ**

**Themes:** Thanksgiving, The Preeminence of Christ, Reconciliation, Paul's Labor for the Church

**Outline:**
1. Greetings and Thanksgiving (1:1-14)
2. The Supremacy of the Son of God (1:15-23)
3. Paul's Labor for the Church (1:24-29)

**Summary:**
Paul gives thanks for the Colossians' faith and prays for their spiritual growth. He presents a powerful poem on the supremacy of Christ as the image of the invisible God, the creator, and the head of the church. He emphasizes that reconciliation comes through Christ's death and discusses his own suffering for the sake of presenting the mystery of Christ.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Fullness in Christ**

**Themes:** Spiritual Fullness, Freedom from Human Regulations, Warning Against False Philosophy

**Outline:**
1. Alive in Christ (2:1-15)
2. Let No One Disqualify You (2:16-23)

**Summary:**
Paul expresses his struggle for the believers, desiring them to be rooted in Christ. He warns them against deceptive philosophies and human traditions. He asserts that in Christ they have been made full and alive, their sins forgiven and spiritual enemies disarmed, rendering legalistic rules and asceticism unnecessary and powerless.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Putting on the New Self**

**Themes:** Things Above, The Old vs. New Self, Rules for Christian Households

**Outline:**
1. Put On the New Self (3:1-17)
2. Rules for Christian Households (3:18-25)

**Summary:**
Believers are instructed to set their minds on heavenly things, since they have been raised with Christ. They must put to death earthly desires and the practices of their old self, instead clothing themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, and love. Paul then provides practical household codes for wives, husbands, children, parents, and slaves.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Further Instructions and Greetings**

**Themes:** Prayer, Wisdom Toward Outsiders, Final Greetings

**Outline:**
1. Further Instructions (4:1-6)
2. Final Greetings (4:7-18)

**Summary:**
Paul concludes his practical instructions by addressing masters, and then urges the church to devote themselves to prayer and to act wisely toward outsiders, letting their speech be gracious. He finishes the letter with a list of personal greetings from and to various co-workers, and a final request for them to remember his chains.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Birth of John the Baptist Foretold**

**Themes:** Prophecy, faith, miraculous birth

**Outline:**
I. Prologue, II. Gabriel appears to Zechariah, III. Gabriel appears to Mary, IV. Mary visits Elizabeth, V. Birth of John

**Summary:**
Luke establishes the historical accuracy of his account. Angels announce the births of John the Baptist and Jesus. Mary rejoices and John is born, followed by Zechariah's prophetic song.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Birth and Childhood of Jesus**

**Themes:** Incarnation, fulfillment, humble beginnings

**Outline:**
I. Jesus' birth in Bethlehem, II. Angels and shepherds, III. Presentation in the temple, IV. The boy Jesus at the temple

**Summary:**
Jesus is born in a manger in Bethlehem. Angels announce his birth to shepherds. Jesus is presented at the temple to Simeon and Anna, and later amazes teachers at the temple at age twelve.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**John the Baptist Prepares the Way**

**Themes:** Repentance, baptism, genealogy

**Outline:**
I. Ministry of John the Baptist, II. Baptism of Jesus, III. Genealogy of Jesus

**Summary:**
John preaches repentance and baptizes Jesus. God affirms Jesus as His Son. The genealogy traces Jesus' lineage back to Adam, emphasizing his role as Savior of all humanity.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Temptation and Early Ministry**

**Themes:** Testing, rejection, authority

**Outline:**
I. Temptation in the wilderness, II. Rejection at Nazareth, III. Healing in Capernaum

**Summary:**
Jesus resists Satan's temptations in the desert. He declares the fulfillment of Isaiah's prophecy in Nazareth but is rejected. He then heals many and drives out demons in Capernaum.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The First Disciples and Early Healings**

**Themes:** Calling, healing, forgiveness

**Outline:**
I. Miraculous catch of fish, II. Healing a leper and paralytic, III. Calling of Levi

**Summary:**
Jesus calls Peter, James, and John after a miraculous catch of fish. He heals a leper and a paralyzed man, demonstrating authority to forgive sins. He calls Levi, a tax collector, and eats with sinners.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Lord of the Sabbath and the Sermon on the Plain**

**Themes:** Sabbath, chosen apostles, ethical living

**Outline:**
I. Lord of the Sabbath, II. The Twelve Apostles, III. Blessings and woes, IV. Love for enemies

**Summary:**
Jesus clashes with Pharisees over the Sabbath. He chooses twelve apostles. He delivers the Sermon on the Plain, teaching about blessings, woes, loving enemies, and judging others.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Faith and Forgiveness**

**Themes:** Authority, compassion, grace

**Outline:**
I. Healing the centurion's servant, II. Raising the widow's son, III. Jesus and John the Baptist, IV. A sinful woman forgiven

**Summary:**
Jesus heals a Roman centurion's servant by word alone and raises a widow's son from the dead. He praises John the Baptist and forgives a sinful woman who washes his feet, teaching about love and forgiveness.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Parables and Miracles**

**Themes:** Word of God, power over nature and demons, faith

**Outline:**
I. Women accompanying Jesus, II. Parable of the Sower, III. Calming the storm, IV. Healing the demon-possessed and the sick

**Summary:**
Jesus travels with his disciples and women who support him. He teaches the Parable of the Sower. He calms a storm, casts out the Legion of demons, heals a bleeding woman, and raises Jairus's daughter.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Sending the Twelve and the Transfiguration**

**Themes:** Mission, identity, cross-bearing

**Outline:**
I. Sending the Twelve, II. Feeding the 5,000, III. Peter's confession and the Transfiguration, IV. Cost of following Jesus

**Summary:**
Jesus sends out the Twelve, feeds five thousand, and is transfigured on a mountain. He predicts his death and teaches about the cost of discipleship as he sets out for Jerusalem.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Mission of the Seventy-Two and the Good Samaritan**

**Themes:** Evangelism, neighborly love, devotion

**Outline:**
I. Sending the Seventy-Two, II. Parable of the Good Samaritan, III. Martha and Mary

**Summary:**
Jesus sends seventy-two disciples on a mission. He teaches the Parable of the Good Samaritan to define who a neighbor is, and visits Martha and Mary, emphasizing listening to his word.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Prayer and Confrontation**

**Themes:** Prayer, spiritual warfare, hypocrisy

**Outline:**
I. The Lord's Prayer, II. Jesus and Beelzebul, III. Woes to the Pharisees

**Summary:**
Jesus teaches the disciples to pray. He defends his power to cast out demons against accusations. He delivers strong woes against the Pharisees and experts in the law for their hypocrisy.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Warnings and Encouragements**

**Themes:** Trust in God, readiness, greed

**Outline:**
I. Warnings against hypocrisy and fear, II. Parable of the Rich Fool, III. Do not worry, IV. Watchfulness

**Summary:**
Jesus warns against hypocrisy and greed, using the Parable of the Rich Fool. He tells his disciples not to worry, to seek God's kingdom, and to be ready for the Son of Man's return.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Repentance and the Kingdom**

**Themes:** Repentance, healing on the Sabbath, kingdom growth

**Outline:**
I. Call to repentance, II. Healing a crippled woman, III. Parables of the Mustard Seed and Yeast, IV. The Narrow Door

**Summary:**
Jesus urges repentance, using the tragedy of the Galileans and the tower of Siloam. He heals a crippled woman on the Sabbath. He teaches parables about the kingdom's growth and the narrow door.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Great Banquet and the Cost of Discipleship**

**Themes:** Humility, inclusion, sacrifice

**Outline:**
I. Healing on the Sabbath, II. Humility and hospitality, III. Parable of the Great Banquet, IV. Cost of discipleship

**Summary:**
Jesus heals a man on the Sabbath and teaches about humility. He tells the Parable of the Great Banquet, showing that the kingdom includes the outcast, and explains the high cost of being his disciple.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Lost and Found Parables**

**Themes:** Joy, repentance, God's seeking love

**Outline:**
I. The Lost Sheep, II. The Lost Coin, III. The Lost Son

**Summary:**
In response to Pharisees grumbling about him eating with sinners, Jesus tells three parables—the Lost Sheep, the Lost Coin, and the Prodigal Son—highlighting heaven's joy when a sinner repents.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Wealth and the Afterlife**

**Themes:** Stewardship, money, eternal consequences

**Outline:**
I. Parable of the Shrewd Manager, II. Teachings on the Law, III. The Rich Man and Lazarus

**Summary:**
Jesus tells the Parable of the Shrewd Manager to teach about the proper use of wealth. He tells the story of the Rich Man and Lazarus, illustrating the eternal consequences of ignoring the poor.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Forgiveness, Faith, and the Kingdom**

**Themes:** Forgiveness, gratitude, the coming Kingdom

**Outline:**
I. Sin, faith, and duty, II. Ten healed of leprosy, III. The coming of the Kingdom

**Summary:**
Jesus teaches about causing others to stumble, forgiveness, and faith. He heals ten lepers, but only one returns to give thanks. He describes the sudden and unmistakable nature of his return.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Prayer, Humility, and the Journey to Jerusalem**

**Themes:** Persistence, humility, salvation

**Outline:**
I. Parable of the Persistent Widow, II. Pharisee and Tax Collector, III. The Rich Young Ruler, IV. Healing a blind beggar

**Summary:**
Jesus teaches persistence in prayer and humility before God. He interacts with little children and a rich ruler, illustrating the difficulty of wealth for salvation, and heals a blind man near Jericho.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Zacchaeus and the Triumphal Entry**

**Themes:** Salvation, stewardship, weeping over Jerusalem

**Outline:**
I. Zacchaeus the tax collector, II. Parable of the Ten Minas, III. The Triumphal Entry, IV. Cleansing the temple

**Summary:**
Jesus brings salvation to the household of Zacchaeus. He teaches the Parable of the Ten Minas about stewardship. He rides into Jerusalem to a welcoming crowd, weeps over the city, and cleanses the temple.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Conflicts in the Temple**

**Themes:** Authority, taxes, resurrection

**Outline:**
I. Jesus' authority questioned, II. Parable of the Tenants, III. Paying taxes to Caesar, IV. Marriage at the resurrection

**Summary:**
Jesus' authority is challenged by the religious leaders. He tells the Parable of the Tenants against them. He answers tricky questions about paying taxes to Caesar and the reality of the resurrection.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Widow's Offering and the End of the Age**

**Themes:** Generosity, tribulation, watchfulness

**Outline:**
I. The Widow's Offering, II. Destruction of the temple foretold, III. Signs of the end of the age

**Summary:**
Jesus commends a poor widow's offering. He predicts the destruction of the temple and describes the signs of the end of the age, urging his followers to be watchful and endure.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Last Supper and Betrayal**

**Themes:** Passover, betrayal, denial

**Outline:**
I. Judas's agreement, II. The Last Supper, III. Prayer on the Mount of Olives, IV. Arrest and Peter's denial

**Summary:**
Jesus celebrates the Last Supper, establishing the New Covenant. He prays in agony on the Mount of Olives. He is betrayed by Judas, arrested, and Peter denies him three times.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Trial and Crucifixion**

**Themes:** Innocence, suffering, death

**Outline:**
I. Jesus before Pilate and Herod, II. The Crucifixion, III. The two criminals, IV. Jesus' death and burial

**Summary:**
Jesus is tried before Pilate and Herod, who find no fault in him, but he is sentenced to death. He is crucified with two criminals, offering salvation to one. He dies and is buried by Joseph of Arimathea.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Resurrection and Ascension**

**Themes:** Resurrection, fulfillment of Scripture, ascension

**Outline:**
I. The empty tomb, II. The road to Emmaus, III. Jesus appears to the disciples, IV. The Ascension

**Summary:**
Women find the tomb empty and are told Jesus has risen. He appears to two disciples on the road to Emmaus, explaining the Scriptures, and then to the eleven. He blesses them and ascends into heaven.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Division in the Church and the Wisdom of God**

**Themes:** Unity, the Cross as foolishness to the world, true wisdom, God's calling.

**Outline:**
1. Greeting and Thanksgiving (1:1-9)
2. Divisions in the Church (1:10-17)
3. Christ the Wisdom and Power of God (1:18-31)

**Summary:**
Paul addresses the divisions among the Corinthians, reminding them that the message of the cross is the true wisdom and power of God, contrasting it with human wisdom.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Proclaiming Christ Crucified and Spiritual Wisdom**

**Themes:** Reliance on the Holy Spirit, divine vs. worldly wisdom, spiritual discernment.

**Outline:**
1. Paul's message and demonstration of the Spirit (2:1-5)
2. The revelation of God's wisdom by the Spirit (2:6-16)

**Summary:**
Paul explains that he relied on the power of the Holy Spirit rather than eloquent speech. True wisdom comes from God's Spirit, which believers have received to understand God's thoughts.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Worldliness and Building on the Foundation of Christ**

**Themes:** Spiritual immaturity, divisions, the church as God's building and temple, judgment of believers' works.

**Outline:**
1. Divisions as a sign of worldliness (3:1-9)
2. Christ as the only foundation (3:10-15)
3. The Church as God's temple (3:16-23)

**Summary:**
Paul rebukes the Corinthians for their fleshly immaturity. He portrays the church as a building founded on Christ, warning that every leader's work will be tested by fire, and affirms that believers are God's temple.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Nature of Apostolic Ministry**

**Themes:** Stewards of God's mysteries, true apostleship, humility, spiritual fatherhood.

**Outline:**
1. Servants of Christ and stewards of mysteries (4:1-5)
2. The apostles' humility contrasted with Corinthian pride (4:6-13)
3. Paul's fatherly warning and impending visit (4:14-21)

**Summary:**
Paul explains the apostles' role as humble servants and stewards, urging the Corinthians to imitate his humility rather than being puffed up with pride.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Dealing with Sexual Immorality in the Church**

**Themes:** Church discipline, purity, dealing with unrepentant sin, the Passover lamb.

**Outline:**
1. A case of incest (5:1-5)
2. The necessity of purging out the old leaven (5:6-8)
3. Clarification on associating with the immoral (5:9-13)

**Summary:**
Paul commands the church to expel a member engaging in blatant incest, emphasizing the need for purity and the principle that a little leaven affects the whole batch of dough.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Lawsuits Among Believers and Sexual Purity**

**Themes:** Resolving disputes internally, avoiding lawsuits, bodies as temples of the Holy Spirit, sexual morality.

**Outline:**
1. Lawsuits before unbelievers (6:1-8)
2. The unrighteous and the kingdom of God (6:9-11)
3. Glorifying God with the body (6:12-20)

**Summary:**
Paul scolds the Corinthians for taking each other to secular courts. He then strongly warns against sexual immorality, reminding them that their bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Principles for Marriage and Singleness**

**Themes:** Marriage, celibacy, divorce, remaining in God's calling, the urgency of the times.

**Outline:**
1. Instructions on marriage and sexual relations (7:1-7)
2. Instructions to the unmarried and widows (7:8-9)
3. Instructions concerning divorce (7:10-16)
4. Living as called (7:17-24)
5. The unmarried and the betrothed (7:25-40)

**Summary:**
Paul answers questions about marriage and singleness, advising both groups. He encourages fidelity in marriage and highlights the benefits of singleness for undistracted devotion to the Lord.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Food Sacrificed to Idols and Christian Liberty**

**Themes:** Christian liberty, avoiding stumbling blocks for weaker believers, love over knowledge.

**Outline:**
1. Knowledge puffs up, love builds up (8:1-3)
2. The reality of idols and the one true God (8:4-6)
3. Forfeiting rights for the sake of the weak (8:7-13)

**Summary:**
Addressing food offered to idols, Paul argues that while idols are nothing, believers must not use their freedom in a way that causes a believer with a sensitive conscience to stumble.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Paul's Apostolic Rights and Self-Denial**

**Themes:** Apostolic rights, self-discipline, giving up rights for the Gospel, running the race.

**Outline:**
1. Paul's rights as an apostle (9:1-14)
2. Paul's renunciation of his rights (9:15-23)
3. The need for spiritual discipline (9:24-27)

**Summary:**
Paul uses himself as an example of willingly giving up legitimate rights (like financial support) for the sake of spreading the Gospel, comparing the Christian life to an athlete's disciplined training.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Warnings from Israel's History and Fleeing Idolatry**

**Themes:** Learning from past failures, avoiding idolatry, doing everything for God's glory.

**Outline:**
1. The example of Israel in the wilderness (10:1-13)
2. The incompatibility of the Lord's table and the table of demons (10:14-22)
3. Doing all to the glory of God (10:23-33)

**Summary:**
Paul warns against falling into the same sins as the Israelites in the wilderness. He urges the Corinthians to flee from idolatry and to prioritize the good of others, doing all to God's glory.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Propriety in Worship and the Lord's Supper**

**Themes:** Head coverings, order in worship, the significance and proper observance of the Lord's Supper.

**Outline:**
1. Head coverings and gender roles in worship (11:1-16)
2. Abuses of the Lord's Supper (11:17-22)
3. The institution of the Lord's Supper (11:23-26)
4. Partaking in a worthy manner (11:27-34)

**Summary:**
Paul addresses propriety in public worship, focusing on head coverings. He then severely corrects their divisive and gluttonous practices at the Lord's Supper, reminding them of its sacred meaning.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Spiritual Gifts and the Body of Christ**

**Themes:** Diversity of spiritual gifts, unity in the church, the body of Christ, interdependence.

**Outline:**
1. The varieties of spiritual gifts given by the same Spirit (12:1-11)
2. The church as one body with many members (12:12-31)

**Summary:**
Paul explains that the Holy Spirit gives diverse gifts for the common good. He illustrates the church as a physical body, where every member is essential and dependent on the others.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Supremacy of Love**

**Themes:** Agape love, the necessity of love over gifts, the permanence of love.

**Outline:**
1. The necessity of love (13:1-3)
2. The characteristics of love (13:4-7)
3. The endurance of love (13:8-13)

**Summary:**
Often called the "Love Chapter," Paul declares that even the greatest spiritual gifts are useless without love. He describes the enduring and selfless nature of true Christian love.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Prophecy, Tongues, and Order in Worship**

**Themes:** Edification of the church, the purpose of prophecy and tongues, orderly worship.

**Outline:**
1. The superiority of prophecy over uninterpreted tongues (14:1-25)
2. Order and edification in church gatherings (14:26-40)

**Summary:**
Paul emphasizes that spiritual gifts must be used to edify the church. He prioritizes prophecy over uninterpreted tongues because it is understandable, and insists that all things in worship be done decently and in order.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Resurrection of Christ and the Dead**

**Themes:** The gospel, the bodily resurrection of Jesus, the future resurrection of believers, victory over death.

**Outline:**
1. The reality of Christ's resurrection (15:1-11)
2. The consequences if there is no resurrection (15:12-19)
3. The order of the resurrection (15:20-34)
4. The nature of the resurrection body (15:35-49)
5. The mystery of the transformation and victory over death (15:50-58)

**Summary:**
Paul defends the crucial doctrine of the resurrection. He proves Christ's resurrection, explains that believers too will be bodily resurrected with imperishable bodies, and celebrates the ultimate defeat of death.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Collection for the Saints and Final Greetings**

**Themes:** Generosity, planning, mutual support, final exhortations, love.

**Outline:**
1. The collection for the Lord's people (16:1-4)
2. Paul's travel plans (16:5-9)
3. Instructions concerning Timothy and Apollos (16:10-12)
4. Final exhortations and greetings (16:13-24)

**Summary:**
Paul gives instructions for a financial collection for the needy believers in Jerusalem, outlines his travel plans, and closes the letter with warm greetings and a final exhortation to stand firm in love.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Prologue and Vision of the Glorified Christ**

**Themes:** Revelation, prophecy, the eternal nature of God, Christ's glory and majesty.

**Outline:**
I. Prologue (1:1-3)
II. Greetings and Doxology (1:4-8)
III. John's Vision of Christ (1:9-20)

**Summary:**
John receives a revelation from Jesus Christ, intended to show God's servants what must soon take place. Exiled on Patmos, John hears a loud voice and turns to see a vision of the glorified Christ standing among seven golden lampstands, holding seven stars. Christ instructs John to write down what he sees and send it to the seven churches.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Messages to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, and Thyatira**

**Themes:** Repentance, endurance in suffering, resisting false teaching, holding fast to faith.

**Outline:**
I. Message to Ephesus (2:1-7)
II. Message to Smyrna (2:8-11)
III. Message to Pergamum (2:12-17)
IV. Message to Thyatira (2:18-29)

**Summary:**
Christ dictates specific messages for four of the seven churches in Asia. He praises Ephesus for their hard work but rebukes them for losing their first love. He encourages Smyrna in their impending persecution. He rebukes Pergamum for tolerating false teachings (Balaam and the Nicolaitans). He rebukes Thyatira for tolerating the false prophetess Jezebel.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Messages to Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea**

**Themes:** Spiritual deadness, divine protection, lukewarm faith, urgent call to repentance.

**Outline:**
I. Message to Sardis (3:1-6)
II. Message to Philadelphia (3:7-13)
III. Message to Laodicea (3:14-22)

**Summary:**
Christ continues His messages to the final three churches. Sardis is rebuked for being spiritually dead despite having a reputation for being alive. Philadelphia is commended for keeping God's word and is promised an open door and protection. Laodicea is strongly rebuked for being spiritually lukewarm, self-sufficient, and blind to their true spiritual poverty.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Throne in Heaven**

**Themes:** God's sovereignty, heavenly worship, God's holiness as Creator.

**Outline:**
I. The Open Door and the Throne (4:1-6a)
II. The Four Living Creatures and Twenty-Four Elders (4:6b-11)

**Summary:**
John is taken up in the Spirit to heaven and sees a door open. He witnesses the glorious throne of God, surrounded by a rainbow, twenty-four elders, and four living creatures. Day and night, they continually worship the Lord God Almighty, praising Him for His holiness and His work of creation.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Scroll and the Lamb**

**Themes:** Christ's worthiness, redemption through His blood, universal worship.

**Outline:**
I. The Sealed Scroll (5:1-4)
II. The Worthy Lamb (5:5-10)
III. All Creation Worships (5:11-14)

**Summary:**
John sees a scroll sealed with seven seals in God's right hand. He weeps because no one is found worthy to open it. An elder tells him that the Lion of the tribe of Judah has triumphed. John then sees a Lamb, looking as if it had been slain. The Lamb takes the scroll, prompting universal worship from the living creatures, elders, angels, and all creation.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Seals**

**Themes:** Divine judgment, conquest, war, famine, death, the cry of the martyrs, the wrath of the Lamb.

**Outline:**
I. The First Four Seals: The Four Horsemen (6:1-8)
II. The Fifth Seal: The Martyrs (6:9-11)
III. The Sixth Seal: Cosmic Disturbances (6:12-17)

**Summary:**
The Lamb begins to open the seals. The first four bring forth the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, representing conquest, war, famine, and death. The fifth seal reveals the souls of martyrs under the altar crying out for justice. The sixth seal causes massive cosmic disturbances and natural disasters, causing all classes of humanity to hide from the wrath of God and the Lamb.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The 144,000 and the Great Multitude**

**Themes:** Divine protection, salvation, ultimate comfort, tribulation.

**Outline:**
I. Sealing of the 144,000 (7:1-8)
II. The Great Multitude in White Robes (7:9-17)

**Summary:**
Before further judgments, angels hold back the four winds of the earth until the servants of God are sealed on their foreheads; John hears their number is 144,000 from the tribes of Israel. Then he sees an uncountable multitude from every nation standing before the throne, clothed in white. They are those who have come out of the great tribulation, and God wipes every tear from their eyes.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Seventh Seal and the Trumpets**

**Themes:** Silence in heaven, prayers of the saints, catastrophic judgments on the earth.

**Outline:**
I. The Seventh Seal and the Golden Censer (8:1-5)
II. The First Four Trumpets (8:6-13)

**Summary:**
When the Lamb opens the seventh seal, there is silence in heaven for about half an hour. An angel offers the prayers of the saints with incense, then hurls the censer to earth, causing thunder and an earthquake. Seven angels prepare to sound their trumpets. The first four trumpets bring devastation to the earth's vegetation, the seas, the fresh waters, and the heavenly bodies.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Fifth and Sixth Trumpets**

**Themes:** Demonic torment, divine limits on evil, judgment, human impenitence.

**Outline:**
I. The Fifth Trumpet: The Plague of Locusts (9:1-12)
II. The Sixth Trumpet: The Angels from the Euphrates (9:13-21)

**Summary:**
The fifth trumpet sounds, releasing a swarm of demonic locusts from the Abyss led by Apollyon to torment those without God's seal for five months. The sixth trumpet releases four angels bound at the Euphrates River, along with a massive demonic cavalry that kills a third of mankind. Despite these severe judgments, the survivors refuse to repent of their idolatry and wickedness.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Angel and the Little Scroll**

**Themes:** Prophetic commission, the mystery of God, sweet and bitter message.

**Outline:**
I. The Mighty Angel (10:1-7)
II. John Eats the Scroll (10:8-11)

**Summary:**
A mighty angel descends from heaven holding a little scroll. He stands on the sea and land, swearing that there will be no more delay and that the mystery of God will be accomplished when the seventh trumpet sounds. John is instructed to take and eat the little scroll; it tastes sweet as honey in his mouth but turns sour in his stomach, symbolizing his renewed prophetic commission.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Two Witnesses and the Seventh Trumpet**

**Themes:** Prophetic witness, martyrdom, vindication, God's eternal reign.

**Outline:**
I. Measuring the Temple (11:1-2)
II. The Two Witnesses (11:3-14)
III. The Seventh Trumpet (11:15-19)

**Summary:**
John is given a reed to measure the temple. Two witnesses are granted power to prophesy for 1,260 days, shutting the sky and bringing plagues. They are ultimately killed by the beast from the Abyss, their bodies left in the street. After three and a half days, God resurrects them and takes them to heaven. The seventh trumpet then sounds, declaring that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of the Lord and of His Christ.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Woman and the Dragon**

**Themes:** Cosmic conflict, Satan's hostility toward God's people, divine protection.

**Outline:**
I. The Woman, the Child, and the Dragon (12:1-6)
II. War in Heaven (12:7-12)
III. The Dragon Persecutes the Woman (12:13-17)

**Summary:**
A great sign appears in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun about to give birth, and a red dragon waiting to devour her child. She gives birth to a male child (Christ), who is snatched up to God. War breaks out in heaven; Michael and his angels defeat the dragon (Satan), throwing him down to earth. Enraged, the dragon pursues the woman and makes war against her offspring.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Two Beasts**

**Themes:** Antichrist, false religion, persecution, the mark of the beast, endurance.

**Outline:**
I. The Beast out of the Sea (13:1-10)
II. The Beast out of the Earth (13:11-18)

**Summary:**
John sees a beast rising out of the sea with seven heads and ten horns, empowered by the dragon to blaspheme God and conquer the saints. The whole world marvels and worships it. A second beast rises from the earth, performing deceptive miracles and forcing all people to worship the first beast. It decrees that everyone must receive a mark (666) on their right hand or forehead to buy or sell.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Lamb and the 144,000, and the Harvest**

**Themes:** Purity, divine judgment, the eternal gospel, reaping the earth.

**Outline:**
I. The Lamb and the 144,000 (14:1-5)
II. The Three Angels' Messages (14:6-13)
III. Reaping the Earth's Harvest (14:14-20)

**Summary:**
John sees the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who are pure and redeemed, singing a new song. Three angels proclaim messages: the eternal gospel, the fall of Babylon, and a warning against taking the mark of the beast. Finally, a vision of two harvests is shown—the Son of Man reaping the grain harvest of the earth, and an angel reaping the grape harvest of God's wrath.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Seven Angels with Seven Plagues**

**Themes:** God's righteous judgments, preparation for wrath, worship.

**Outline:**
I. The Song of Moses and the Lamb (15:1-4)
II. Preparation of the Bowls of Wrath (15:5-8)

**Summary:**
John sees seven angels holding the seven last plagues. Those who have been victorious over the beast stand beside a sea of glass, singing the song of Moses and the Lamb, praising God's justice. The temple in heaven is opened, and the seven angels receive seven golden bowls filled with the wrath of God. The temple fills with smoke, and no one can enter until the plagues are completed.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Seven Bowls of God's Wrath**

**Themes:** Final and complete judgment, human stubbornness, Armageddon.

**Outline:**
I. The First Three Bowls (16:1-7)
II. The Next Three Bowls (16:8-16)
III. The Seventh Bowl (16:17-21)

**Summary:**
A loud voice commands the seven angels to pour out the bowls of God's wrath. The plagues bring sores, turn the seas and rivers to blood, scorch people with fire, and plunge the beast's kingdom into darkness. Despite the agony, people refuse to repent. Demonic spirits gather the kings of the world for the battle of Armageddon. The final bowl causes an unprecedented global earthquake and massive hailstones.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Great Prostitute and the Beast**

**Themes:** Spiritual adultery, oppressive world systems, the allure and doom of Babylon.

**Outline:**
I. Vision of the Great Prostitute (17:1-6)
II. The Mystery Explained (17:7-18)

**Summary:**
An angel shows John the judgment of the great prostitute, Babylon, who sits on many waters and rides a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns. She is drunk with the blood of the saints. The angel explains that the beast's heads represent kings/mountains and the horns represent future kings who will ally with the beast, eventually turning against the prostitute to destroy her, fulfilling God's purpose.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Fall of Babylon**

**Themes:** Economic collapse, divine justice, separation from worldly corruption.

**Outline:**
I. The Announcement of Babylon's Fall (18:1-3)
II. Call to Separate from Her (18:4-8)
III. Lament over Babylon (18:9-19)
IV. Heaven Rejoices (18:20-24)

**Summary:**
A mighty angel declares that Babylon the Great has fallen. A voice from heaven urges God's people to flee from her to avoid sharing in her sins and plagues. The kings, merchants, and sailors of the earth mourn her sudden destruction because their source of wealth is gone. In contrast, heaven and the saints are called to rejoice over her righteous judgment.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Rejoicing in Heaven and the Rider on the White Horse**

**Themes:** Praise, the marriage of the Lamb, righteous warfare, victory of Christ.

**Outline:**
I. Hallelujah Chorus (19:1-5)
II. The Marriage Supper of the Lamb (19:6-10)
III. The Rider on the White Horse Defeats the Beast (19:11-21)

**Summary:**
A great multitude in heaven shouts 'Hallelujah!' praising God for judging the prostitute and bringing about the marriage of the Lamb to His prepared bride. John then sees heaven open and Christ appearing as a rider on a white horse, named Faithful and True, the Word of God. He leads the armies of heaven to strike down the nations, capturing the beast and the false prophet, throwing them into the lake of fire.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Millennium and the Final Judgment**

**Themes:** The binding of Satan, Christ's reign, final defeat of evil, the Great White Throne.

**Outline:**
I. Satan Bound and the Millennial Reign (20:1-6)
II. Satan's Final Defeat (20:7-10)
III. The Great White Throne Judgment (20:11-15)

**Summary:**
An angel binds Satan in the Abyss for a thousand years, during which resurrected saints reign with Christ. Afterward, Satan is released and deceives the nations (Gog and Magog) for one final battle, but fire from heaven consumes them, and Satan is thrown into the lake of fire permanently. Then, all the dead stand before the Great White Throne for final judgment; anyone whose name is not in the book of life is cast into the lake of fire.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The New Heaven and the New Earth**

**Themes:** Restoration, eternal dwelling of God with humanity, glory of the New Jerusalem.

**Outline:**
I. All Things Made New (21:1-8)
II. The New Jerusalem Described (21:9-21)
III. The Glory of the City (21:22-27)

**Summary:**
John sees a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth have passed away. The Holy City, the New Jerusalem, descends from heaven. God dwells intimately with His people, wiping away every tear and eliminating death and pain. An angel shows John the city's magnificent structure—its glowing jasper walls, pearly gates, and foundations of precious stones. It needs no sun or moon, for God's glory illuminates it.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Eden Restored and Jesus Is Coming**

**Themes:** Eternal life, the river of life, the imminent return of Christ, invitation and warning.

**Outline:**
I. The River and Tree of Life (22:1-5)
II. Final Reminders and Exhortations (22:6-17)
III. Final Warning and Benediction (22:18-21)

**Summary:**
The angel shows John the river of the water of life flowing from God's throne, with the tree of life bearing fruit on its banks, reversing the curse of Eden. God's servants will see His face and reign forever. The book closes with strong affirmations that Jesus is coming soon. A final invitation is given to all who are thirsty to take the free gift of the water of life, accompanied by a warning not to add or take away from the prophecy.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Faith and Wisdom**

**Themes:** Trials, Wisdom, Faith, Hearing and Doing

**Outline:**
I. Greetings (1:1)
II. Faith and Wisdom in Trials (1:2-18)
III. Hearing and Doing the Word (1:19-27)

**Summary:**
James encourages believers to rejoice in trials, ask God for wisdom, and ensure that their faith is active through doing the word, not just hearing it.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Faith Without Works is Dead**

**Themes:** Favoritism, Active Faith, Good Works

**Outline:**
I. Warning Against Partiality (2:1-13)
II. Faith Without Works is Dead (2:14-26)

**Summary:**
James warns against showing favoritism to the rich and argues that genuine faith is necessarily accompanied by righteous works, illustrating this with Abraham and Rahab.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Taming the Tongue**

**Themes:** Speech, Heavenly Wisdom

**Outline:**
I. Taming the Tongue (3:1-12)
II. Two Kinds of Wisdom (3:13-18)

**Summary:**
James highlights the disproportionate power of the tongue to cause harm and contrasts earthly, demonic wisdom with peace-loving, heavenly wisdom.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Submission to God**

**Themes:** Humility, Worldliness, Judging Others, Boasting

**Outline:**
I. Warning Against Worldliness (4:1-12)
II. Warning Against Boasting (4:13-17)

**Summary:**
James addresses conflicts caused by worldly desires, calling for humility and submission to God. He also warns against arrogant boasting about tomorrow.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Patience and Prayer**

**Themes:** Wealth, Patience, Prayer, Confession

**Outline:**
I. Warning to the Rich (5:1-6)
II. Patience in Suffering (5:7-12)
III. The Prayer of Faith (5:13-20)

**Summary:**
James pronounces judgment on oppressive rich people, encourages patience among suffering believers until the Lord's return, and emphasizes the power of faithful prayer and confession.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**A Living Hope**

**Themes:** Hope, Salvation, Holiness

**Outline:**
I. Greetings (1:1-2)
II. A Living Hope (1:3-12)
III. A Call to Holy Living (1:13-25)

**Summary:**
Peter praises God for the living hope and future inheritance of believers. He urges them to live holy lives in reverent fear, having been redeemed by Christ's blood.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Living Stones and Submission**

**Themes:** Spiritual Growth, Submission, Suffering

**Outline:**
I. The Living Stone and a Chosen People (2:1-10)
II. Living Honorably (2:11-12)
III. Submission to Authority (2:13-25)

**Summary:**
Peter describes believers as living stones built into a spiritual house. He instructs them to submit to human authorities and endure unjust suffering, following Christ's example.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Wives, Husbands, and Righteous Suffering**

**Themes:** Marriage, Righteousness, Suffering for Doing Good

**Outline:**
I. Wives and Husbands (3:1-7)
II. Suffering for Righteousness (3:8-22)

**Summary:**
Peter provides instructions for godly marriages. He encourages believers to pursue peace and to be prepared to suffer for doing good, just as Christ suffered for sins.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Living for God**

**Themes:** Stewardship, Suffering as a Christian

**Outline:**
I. Living for God (4:1-11)
II. Suffering for Being a Christian (4:12-19)

**Summary:**
Peter urges believers to live for God's will rather than human desires, to use their spiritual gifts to serve others, and to rejoice when participating in the sufferings of Christ.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Shepherding the Flock**

**Themes:** Leadership, Humility, Vigilance

**Outline:**
I. To the Elders and the Flock (5:1-11)
II. Final Greetings (5:12-14)

**Summary:**
Peter instructs elders to shepherd God's flock willingly and humbly. He advises all believers to be humble, cast their anxieties on God, and remain vigilant against the devil.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Making Calling and Election Sure**

**Themes:** Christian Virtues, Prophecy, Truth

**Outline:**
I. Greetings (1:1-2)
II. Making Calling and Election Sure (1:3-15)
III. The Prophetic Word Confirmed (1:16-21)

**Summary:**
Peter exhorts believers to supplement their faith with virtue and knowledge to make their calling sure. He affirms the reliability of the prophetic word and his eyewitness testimony of Christ's majesty.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**False Prophets and Teachers**

**Themes:** False Teaching, Judgment, Depravity

**Outline:**
I. The Danger of False Teachers (2:1-3)
II. God's Judgment on the Wicked (2:4-10a)
III. Description of False Teachers (2:10b-22)

**Summary:**
Peter warns of false teachers who will secretly introduce destructive heresies. He uses historical examples to show that God will judge the unrighteous and rescue the godly.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Day of the Lord**

**Themes:** The Second Coming, Patience, Holiness

**Outline:**
I. The Certainty of Christ's Coming (3:1-13)
II. Final Exhortations (3:14-18)

**Summary:**
Peter addresses scoffers who doubt the Second Coming, explaining that God's delay is due to His patience, desiring all to repent. He urges believers to live holy lives in anticipation of the new heavens and new earth.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Walking in the Light**

**Themes:** Incarnation, Light vs. Darkness, Forgiveness

**Outline:**
I. The Word of Life (1:1-4)
II. Walking in the Light (1:5-10)

**Summary:**
John proclaims the reality of the incarnate Christ and declares that God is light. He explains that fellowship with God requires walking in the light and confessing sins to receive forgiveness.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Love and Antichrists**

**Themes:** Obedience, Love for the World, Antichrists

**Outline:**
I. Christ Our Advocate (2:1-6)
II. The New Commandment (2:7-14)
III. Do Not Love the World (2:15-17)
IV. Warning Against Antichrists (2:18-29)

**Summary:**
John presents Christ as our advocate and emphasizes that knowing God involves keeping His commandments. He warns against loving the world and cautions believers about antichrists who deny Jesus.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Children of God**

**Themes:** Love, Righteousness, Confidence

**Outline:**
I. Children of God (3:1-10)
II. Love One Another (3:11-24)

**Summary:**
John marvels at the love that calls believers children of God. He contrasts children of God with children of the devil, stating that those born of God practice righteousness and genuinely love their brothers and sisters.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Testing the Spirits and God's Love**

**Themes:** Truth, God is Love, Fearless Love

**Outline:**
I. Testing the Spirits (4:1-6)
II. God is Love (4:7-21)

**Summary:**
John instructs believers to test spirits to see if they acknowledge Jesus came in the flesh. He profoundly states that God is love, and since God loved us, we also ought to love one another, which casts out fear.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Faith and Eternal Life**

**Themes:** Faith, Testimony, Eternal Life

**Outline:**
I. Overcoming the World (5:1-5)
II. Testimony Concerning the Son (5:6-12)
III. That You May Know (5:13-21)

**Summary:**
John emphasizes that faith in Jesus as the Son of God is the victory that overcomes the world. He writes so that believers may know they have eternal life and have confidence in prayer.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Walking in Truth and Love**

**Themes:** Truth, Love, False Teachers

**Outline:**
I. Greeting (1-3)
II. Walking in Truth and Love (4-6)
III. Warning Against Deceivers (7-11)
IV. Final Greetings (12-13)

**Summary:**
John writes to the 'elect lady and her children,' rejoicing that they are walking in truth. He exhorts them to love one another and warns them not to show hospitality to false teachers who deny the incarnation.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Hospitality and Opposition**

**Themes:** Hospitality, Faithfulness, Pride

**Outline:**
I. Greeting to Gaius (1-4)
II. Praise for Gaius's Hospitality (5-8)
III. Diotrephes's Opposition (9-10)
IV. Demetrius's Good Testimony and Conclusion (11-15)

**Summary:**
John commends Gaius for his faithful hospitality to traveling missionaries. He contrasts this with the prideful and obstructive behavior of Diotrephes, while affirming the good testimony of Demetrius.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Contending for the Faith**

**Themes:** False Teachers, Judgment, Perseverance

**Outline:**
I. Greeting (1-2)
II. The Call to Contend for the Faith (3-4)
III. God's Judgment on the Ungodly (5-16)
IV. Call to Persevere (17-23)
V. Doxology (24-25)

**Summary:**
Jude urgently appeals to believers to contend for the faith against ungodly intruders who pervert God's grace. He reminds them of past judgments and urges them to persevere in God's love, ending with a magnificent doxology.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Christ's Superiority to the Angels**

**Themes:** Christology, Revelation, Superiority of Jesus, Angels

**Outline:**
I. God's Final Word in His Son (1:1-3)
II. Christ's Superiority to the Angels Declared (1:4-14)

**Summary:**
The author establishes the supreme supremacy of Jesus Christ. God, who formerly spoke through prophets, has now spoken through His Son, who is the exact representation of His being. The chapter uses numerous Old Testament quotations to demonstrate that Jesus is exalted far above the angels, possessing an eternal throne and an unchangeable nature.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Warning to Pay Attention and Christ's Identification with Humanity**

**Themes:** Salvation, Warning, Incarnation, Atonement, Suffering

**Outline:**
I. Warning Against Drifting (2:1-4)
II. The Incarnation: Lower Than Angels for a Time (2:5-9)
III. The Pioneer of Salvation Made Perfect Through Suffering (2:10-18)

**Summary:**
A warning is given not to neglect so great a salvation. The author then explains why Jesus, who is greater than angels, had to become a human, lower than the angels for a time. By partaking in flesh and blood, Jesus conquered death and the devil, becoming a merciful and faithful high priest capable of sympathizing with human weakness and suffering.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Jesus Greater Than Moses and a Warning Against Unbelief**

**Themes:** Faithfulness, Superiority to Moses, Unbelief, Rest

**Outline:**
I. Jesus the Apostle and High Priest Greater Than Moses (3:1-6)
II. Warning Against an Unbelieving Heart (3:7-19)

**Summary:**
Jesus is presented as greater than Moses. While Moses was a faithful servant in God's house, Jesus is the faithful Son over God's house. Following this comparison, a stern warning, drawn from Psalm 95, urges believers not to harden their hearts in rebellion as the Israelites did in the wilderness, which led to their exclusion from God's rest due to unbelief.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Entering God's Rest and the Great High Priest**

**Themes:** Sabbath Rest, Word of God, High Priesthood, Grace

**Outline:**
I. The Promise of God's Rest (4:1-13)
II. Jesus the Great High Priest (4:14-16)

**Summary:**
The promise of entering God's rest remains open, referring to a spiritual rest rather than just physical settlement in Canaan or the Sabbath day. Believers are urged to strive to enter that rest and avoid the disobedience of their ancestors. The chapter highlights the living and active nature of God's Word, and concludes by introducing Jesus as the Great High Priest who sympathizes with our weaknesses, encouraging us to approach the throne of grace with confidence.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Christ the High Priest and a Warning Against Immaturity**

**Themes:** High Priesthood, Melchizedek, Obedience, Spiritual Immaturity

**Outline:**
I. Qualifications of a High Priest (5:1-4)
II. Jesus Appointed as High Priest (5:5-10)
III. Warning Against Spiritual Immaturity (5:11-14)

**Summary:**
The qualifications for the earthly high priesthood are outlined and applied to Jesus, whom God appointed according to the order of Melchizedek. Though He was a Son, Jesus learned obedience through suffering and became the source of eternal salvation. The author pauses the theological argument to rebuke the readers for their spiritual immaturity and inability to digest solid theological 'food'.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Warning Against Falling Away and the Certainty of God's Promise**

**Themes:** Apostasy, Perseverance, God's Promises, Hope

**Outline:**
I. Moving Toward Maturity (6:1-3)
II. Warning Against Falling Away (6:4-12)
III. The Certainty of God's Promise (6:13-20)

**Summary:**
The readers are exhorted to press on to maturity. A severe warning is issued about the impossibility of restoring to repentance those who have truly fallen away and crucified the Son of God all over again. However, the author expresses confidence in the readers' salvation, encouraging them to show diligence. The chapter emphasizes the unchangeable nature of God's promises, guaranteed by His oath, providing a sure and steadfast anchor for the soul in Jesus.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Priesthood of Melchizedek**

**Themes:** Melchizedek, Superiority of Christ's Priesthood, Old Covenant Obsolete

**Outline:**
I. Melchizedek the Priest-King (7:1-10)
II. Jesus Like Melchizedek (7:11-22)
III. The Superiority of the Permanent Priesthood (7:23-28)

**Summary:**
The historical figure of Melchizedek is explored to demonstrate that his priesthood is superior to the Levitical priesthood, as even Abraham paid tithes to him. Consequently, Jesus, being a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek, guarantees a better covenant. Unlike Levitical priests who die and need to offer sacrifices for their own sins, Jesus lives forever, is perfectly holy, and offered Himself once for all.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The High Priest of a New Covenant**

**Themes:** New Covenant, Old Covenant, Heavenly Sanctuary

**Outline:**
I. Christ's Ministry in the True Tabernacle (8:1-6)
II. The New Covenant Replaces the Old (8:7-13)

**Summary:**
The main point of the preceding arguments is stated: we have a High Priest who sits at the right hand of God in the heavenly sanctuary. His ministry is superior because He mediates a better covenant founded on better promises. Quoting Jeremiah 31, the author explains that the first covenant was flawed, and God has established a New Covenant where His laws are written on the mind and heart, rendering the old covenant obsolete.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Earthly Sanctuary and the Blood of Christ**

**Themes:** Tabernacle, Blood Atonement, Forgiveness, Christ's Sacrifice

**Outline:**
I. Worship in the Earthly Tabernacle (9:1-10)
II. The Blood of Christ in the Heavenly Sanctuary (9:11-28)

**Summary:**
The author describes the earthly tabernacle and its rituals under the Old Covenant, noting that they were merely temporary copies of heavenly realities and could not clear the conscience. In contrast, Christ entered the true, heavenly sanctuary not with the blood of animals, but with His own blood, securing eternal redemption. His one-time sacrifice takes away the sins of many and brings the New Covenant into effect.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Christ's Perfect Sacrifice and the Call to Persevere**

**Themes:** Once-for-All Sacrifice, Forgiveness, Perseverance, Judgment

**Outline:**
I. The Inadequacy of Animal Sacrifices (10:1-4)
II. Christ's Sacrifice Once for All (10:5-18)
III. Call to Persevere in Faith (10:19-39)

**Summary:**
The law is depicted as a shadow, incapable of making worshippers perfect. Christ's single sacrifice of Himself did what the repetitive animal sacrifices could not, perfecting for all time those who are being sanctified. Since sins are forgiven, there is no longer a need for sin offerings. Believers are encouraged to draw near to God with sincere hearts, hold unswervingly to hope, and meet together. A stern warning against willful sin follows, emphasizing the fearful prospect of judgment, concluding with an exhortation to endure by faith.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Hall of Faith**

**Themes:** Faith, Examples of the Old Testament, Endurance, Promise

**Outline:**
I. The Nature of Faith (11:1-3)
II. Examples of Faith from Abel to Abraham (11:4-19)
III. Examples of Faith from Isaac to Rahab (11:20-31)
IV. Summary of the Triumphs and Sufferings of Faith (11:32-40)

**Summary:**
Faith is defined as confidence in what is hoped for and assurance about what is not seen. The chapter lists a magnificent 'Hall of Faith' highlighting Old Testament figures—like Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Rahab—who demonstrated extraordinary trust in God's promises, often facing great adversity. Though none received what was fully promised in their lifetime, their enduring faith serves as a profound testimony and inspiration for believers.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Enduring Discipline and Worshipping with Reverence**

**Themes:** Endurance, Discipline, Holiness, Two Mountains

**Outline:**
I. Run the Race and Endure Discipline (12:1-13)
II. Warning Against Rejecting God's Grace (12:14-17)
III. Mount Sinai vs. Mount Zion (12:18-29)

**Summary:**
Surrounded by the 'cloud of witnesses' from chapter 11, believers are urged to throw off sin and run with perseverance, fixing their eyes on Jesus. Suffering is to be understood as the loving discipline of a Father shaping His children for holiness. Believers are warned not to be like Esau, but to pursue peace and holiness. The author contrasts the terrifying approach to God at Mount Sinai with the joyful assembly at heavenly Mount Zion, urging reverence and awe since God is a consuming fire.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Concluding Exhortations and Benediction**

**Themes:** Love, Hospitality, Leaders, Unchanging Christ, Blessing

**Outline:**
I. Exhortations for Christian Living (13:1-6)
II. Following the Leaders and Christ (13:7-17)
III. Request for Prayer, Benediction, and Greetings (13:18-25)

**Summary:**
The epistle concludes with practical exhortations: show brotherly love, practice hospitality, remember those in prison, honor marriage, and avoid the love of money. Believers are told to remember their leaders and hold to the truth that 'Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.' After urging them to continually offer a sacrifice of praise, the author concludes with a request for prayer, a beautiful benediction for their equipping in every good thing, and final greetings.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Genealogy and Birth of Jesus Christ**

**Themes:** Fulfillment of prophecy, Davidic lineage, Divine origin, Emmanuel (God with us)

**Outline:**
I. The Genealogy of Jesus (1:1-17)
II. The Birth of Jesus (1:18-25)

**Summary:**
Matthew begins his Gospel by tracing the lineage of Jesus back to Abraham and David, establishing his messianic credentials. The narrative then shifts to the miraculous conception of Jesus through the Holy Spirit. An angel appears to Joseph in a dream, reassuring him to take Mary as his wife and revealing that the child will save his people from their sins.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Visit of the Magi and the Flight to Egypt**

**Themes:** Jesus as King of the Jews, Gentile recognition, Hostility to the Messiah, Divine protection, Fulfillment of prophecy

**Outline:**
I. The Visit of the Wise Men (2:1-12)
II. The Flight to Egypt (2:13-15)
III. Herod Kills the Children (2:16-18)
IV. The Return to Nazareth (2:19-23)

**Summary:**
Magi from the East arrive in Jerusalem seeking the newborn King of the Jews, alarming King Herod. Guided by a star, they find Jesus in Bethlehem and worship him. Warned in a dream, they bypass Herod on their return. Joseph is also warned in a dream to flee to Egypt with Mary and Jesus to escape Herod's massacre of the infants. After Herod's death, the holy family settles in Nazareth.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Ministry of John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus**

**Themes:** Repentance, The Kingdom of Heaven, Preparation, Trinity, Divine endorsement

**Outline:**
I. John the Baptist Prepares the Way (3:1-12)
II. The Baptism of Jesus (3:13-17)

**Summary:**
John the Baptist preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judea, announcing the imminent arrival of the Kingdom of Heaven and baptizing people in the Jordan River. He sharply rebukes the Pharisees and Sadducees. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John. As Jesus comes up from the water, the Spirit of God descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven declares him to be God's beloved Son.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Temptation of Jesus and the Beginning of His Ministry**

**Themes:** Temptation, Obedience, Word of God, Kingdom of Heaven, Calling of disciples, Healing

**Outline:**
I. The Temptation of Jesus (4:1-11)
II. Jesus Begins His Ministry in Galilee (4:12-17)
III. Jesus Calls the First Disciples (4:18-22)
IV. Jesus Ministers to Great Crowds (4:23-25)

**Summary:**
Jesus is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, where he fasts for forty days and is tempted by Satan. Jesus defeats each temptation by quoting Scripture. After John is arrested, Jesus begins preaching repentance in Galilee. He calls Peter, Andrew, James, and John to be "fishers of men." His ministry of teaching, preaching, and healing attracts large crowds from various regions.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Sermon on the Mount: The Beatitudes and the Higher Righteousness**

**Themes:** Blessing, Kingdom values, Fulfillment of the Law, True righteousness, Love for enemies

**Outline:**
I. The Beatitudes (5:1-12)
II. Salt and Light (5:13-16)
III. Christ Fulfills the Law (5:17-20)
IV. Teaching on Anger, Lust, and Divorce (5:21-32)
V. Teaching on Oaths, Retaliation, and Love for Enemies (5:33-48)

**Summary:**
Jesus ascends a mountain and begins his most famous discourse, opening with the Beatitudes, which describe the character and blessedness of Kingdom citizens. He calls his followers the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Jesus asserts that he came to fulfill the Law, not abolish it, and then intensifies several Old Testament commands, focusing on the heart's intent regarding anger, lust, divorce, oaths, retaliation, and loving one's enemies.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Sermon on the Mount: Authentic Piety and Trust in God**

**Themes:** Hypocrisy, The Lord's Prayer, Fasting, True treasure, Anxiety, Trusting God's provision

**Outline:**
I. Giving to the Needy (6:1-4)
II. The Lord's Prayer (6:5-15)
III. Fasting (6:16-18)
IV. Treasures in Heaven (6:19-24)
V. Do Not Be Anxious (6:25-34)

**Summary:**
Jesus warns against performing acts of righteousness—giving, praying, and fasting—to be seen by others, teaching instead to do them in secret for God's reward. He provides the Lord's Prayer as a model. He exhorts his followers to lay up treasures in heaven rather than on earth, declaring that one cannot serve both God and money. Finally, he commands them not to worry about basic needs, urging them to seek first God's kingdom and righteousness.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Sermon on the Mount: Judgment, Discernment, and the Two Foundations**

**Themes:** Judging others, Prayer, The Golden Rule, False prophets, True discipleship, Obedience

**Outline:**
I. Judging Others (7:1-6)
II. Ask, Seek, Knock (7:7-11)
III. The Golden Rule (7:12)
IV. The Narrow Gate (7:13-14)
V. A Tree and Its Fruit (7:15-20)
VI. I Never Knew You (7:21-23)
VII. Build Your House on the Rock (7:24-29)

**Summary:**
Jesus concludes the Sermon on the Mount by warning against hypocritical judgment and encouraging persistent prayer. He summarizes the Law and Prophets with the Golden Rule. He describes the narrow gate that leads to life and warns against false prophets, identifiable by their fruit. Emphasizing obedience, he states that not all who say "Lord, Lord" will enter the kingdom. He illustrates his teaching with the parable of the wise and foolish builders, leaving the crowds astonished at his authority.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Miracles of Healing and Authority over Nature and Demons**

**Themes:** Authority of Jesus, Compassion, Faith, Discipleship, Messianic power

**Outline:**
I. Jesus Cleanses a Leper (8:1-4)
II. The Faith of the Centurion (8:5-13)
III. Jesus Heals Many (8:14-17)
IV. The Cost of Following Jesus (8:18-22)
V. Jesus Calms a Storm (8:23-27)
VI. Jesus Heals Two Men with Demons (8:28-34)

**Summary:**
Following his sermon, Jesus demonstrates his authority through a series of miracles. He heals a leper, a centurion's paralyzed servant (praising the Gentile's great faith), and Peter's mother-in-law, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy about bearing diseases. He warns of the cost of discipleship. On the Sea of Galilee, he calms a violent storm with a word, marveling his disciples. In the region of the Gadarenes, he delivers two violent demon-possessed men, sending the demons into a herd of pigs.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Further Miracles, Forgiveness, and the Call of Matthew**

**Themes:** Authority to forgive sins, Eating with sinners, Fasting, Healing, Compassion for the lost

**Outline:**
I. Jesus Heals a Paralytic (9:1-8)
II. Jesus Calls Matthew (9:9-13)
III. A Question About Fasting (9:14-17)
IV. A Girl Restored to Life and a Woman Healed (9:18-26)
V. Jesus Heals Two Blind Men (9:27-31)
VI. Jesus Heals a Man Unable to Speak (9:32-34)
VII. The Harvest is Plentiful (9:35-38)

**Summary:**
Jesus heals a paralytic, explicitly claiming the authority to forgive sins. He calls Matthew, a tax collector, to follow him, and defends dining with sinners to the Pharisees. After answering a question about fasting using the analogy of new wineskins, he raises a ruler's daughter from the dead and heals a woman with a bleeding disorder. He also restores sight to two blind men and casts out a mute demon. Moved by compassion for the crowds, he urges prayer for more laborers for the spiritual harvest.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Commissioning of the Twelve Apostles**

**Themes:** Apostolic authority, Mission, Persecution, Fearlessness, Cost of discipleship, Reward

**Outline:**
I. The Twelve Apostles (10:1-4)
II. Jesus Sends Out the Twelve (10:5-15)
III. Persecution Will Come (10:16-25)
IV. Have No Fear (10:26-33)
V. Not Peace, but a Sword (10:34-39)
VI. Rewards (10:40-42)

**Summary:**
Jesus summons his twelve disciples, giving them authority over unclean spirits and diseases. He sends them out to the "lost sheep of Israel" to proclaim the kingdom and heal. He provides detailed instructions, warning them of impending persecution and trials but encouraging them not to fear those who can only kill the body. He emphasizes that loyalty to him must surpass family ties, taking up one's cross, and promises rewards to those who receive his messengers.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Jesus and John the Baptist; The Yoke of Christ**

**Themes:** Doubt, Identity of Jesus and John, Unbelief, Judgment, Rest, Revelation

**Outline:**
I. Messengers from John the Baptist (11:1-6)
II. Jesus Praises John the Baptist (11:7-19)
III. Woe to Unrepentant Cities (11:20-24)
IV. Come to Me, and I Will Give You Rest (11:25-30)

**Summary:**
John the Baptist, now imprisoned, sends disciples to ask if Jesus is truly the awaited one. Jesus answers by pointing to his miracles. Jesus praises John as the greatest prophet but notes the generation's rejection of both John's asceticism and Jesus' joyful ministry. He denounces the Galilean cities where he performed many miracles for their lack of repentance. Finally, he praises the Father for revealing truth to the humble and offers his easy yoke and rest to the weary and burdened.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**Sabbath Controversies and the Unpardonable Sin**

**Themes:** Lord of the Sabbath, Mercy over sacrifice, Blasphemy against the Spirit, Sign of Jonah, True family

**Outline:**
I. Jesus Is Lord of the Sabbath (12:1-8)
II. A Man with a Withered Hand (12:9-14)
III. God's Chosen Servant (12:15-21)
IV. Blasphemy Against the Holy Spirit (12:22-32)
V. A Tree Is Known by Its Fruit (12:33-37)
VI. The Sign of Jonah (12:38-42)
VII. Return of an Unclean Spirit (12:43-45)
VIII. Jesus' Mother and Brothers (12:46-50)

**Summary:**
Conflict with the Pharisees escalates over Sabbath observance when the disciples pluck grain and Jesus heals a man with a withered hand, leading the Pharisees to plot his death. Fulfilling prophecy as God's gentle servant, Jesus heals a demon-oppressed man. When Pharisees attribute his power to Beelzebul, he warns that blasphemy against the Spirit is unforgivable. He refuses to give a sign except the "sign of Jonah" and redefines his family as those who do the will of his Father.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Parables of the Kingdom**

**Themes:** Kingdom of Heaven, Mystery, Receptivity of the heart, Judgment, Hidden treasure

**Outline:**
I. The Parable of the Sower (13:1-9, 18-23)
II. The Purpose of Parables (13:10-17)
III. The Parable of the Weeds (13:24-30, 36-43)
IV. The Mustard Seed and the Leaven (13:31-33)
V. Hidden Treasure and the Pearl of Great Value (13:44-46)
VI. The Parable of the Net (13:47-50)
VII. New and Old Treasures (13:51-52)
VIII. Jesus Rejected at Nazareth (13:53-58)

**Summary:**
Jesus teaches the crowds from a boat using a series of parables about the Kingdom of Heaven. The Parable of the Sower illustrates different responses to the gospel. He explains that parables reveal truth to disciples but hide it from the hard-hearted. Further parables—the Weeds, Mustard Seed, Leaven, Hidden Treasure, Pearl, and Net—describe the kingdom's growth, extraordinary value, and the final judgment separating the righteous from the wicked. He is subsequently rejected in his hometown of Nazareth due to their unbelief.

entries.author: The Blessed Bible Study Guide
entries.text:
**The Death of John the Baptist, Feeding the 5,000, and Walking on Water**

**Themes:** Martyrdom, Divine provision, Miracles, Faith and doubt, Worship

**Outline:**
I. The Death of John the Baptist (14:1-12)
II. Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand (14:13-21)
III. Jesus Walks on the Water (14:22-33)
IV. Jesus Heals the Sick in Gennesaret (14:34-36)

**Summary:**
Herod Antipas mistakenly believes Jesus is a resurrected John the Baptist, whom Herod had recently beheaded at the request of Herodias's daughter. Upon hearing of John's death, Jesus withdraws but is followed by crowds. Moved by compassion, he miraculously feeds 5,000 men (plus women and children) with five loaves and two fish.
